name: mix

return.doc: The interpolated value. vec_type *mix*(vec_type a, vec_type b, vec_bool_type c) 🔗 <#shader- func-mix> Selects either value `a` or value `b` based on the value of `c`. For a component of `c` that is false, the corresponding component of `a` is returned. For a component of `c` that is true, the corresponding component of `b` is returned. Components of `a` and `b` that are not selected are allowed to be invalid floating-point values and will have no effect on the results. If `a`, `b`, and `c` are vector types the operation is performed component-wise <#shading-componentwise>. ie. `mix(vec2(42, 314), vec2(9.8, 6e23), bvec2(true, false)))` will return `vec2(9.8, 314)`. The interpolated value.

arguments.name: c
arguments.doc: The value to use to interpolate between `a` and `b`. The value used to select between `a` and `b`.

doc: Performs a linear interpolation between `a` and `b` using `c` to weight between them. Computed as `a * (1 - c) + b * c`. class_%40globalscope.html#class-globalscope-method-lerp> in GDScript.

name: fma

arguments.name: a
arguments.doc: The first value to be multiplied.

arguments.name: b
arguments.doc: The second value to be multiplied.

arguments.name: c
arguments.doc: The value to be added to the result.

doc: Performs, where possible, a fused multiply-add operation, returning `a * b + c`. In use cases where the return value is eventually consumed by a variable declared as precise: * `fma()` is considered a single operation, whereas the expression `a * b + c` consumed by a variable declared as precise is considered two operations. * The precision of `fma()` can differ from the precision of the expression `a * b + c`. * `fma()` will be computed with the same precision as any other `fma()` consumed by a precise variable, giving invariant results for the same input values of a, b and c. Otherwise, in the absence of precise consumption, there are no special constraints on the number of operations or difference in precision between `fma()` and the expression `a * b + c`.

name: step

arguments.name: b

doc: Generates a step function by comparing b to a. Equivalent to `if (b < a) { return 0.0; } else { return 1.0; }`. For element i of the return value, 0.0 is returned if b[i] < a[i], and 1.0 is returned otherwise.

name: smoothstep

arguments.name: a
arguments.doc: The value of the lower edge of the Hermite function.

arguments.name: b
arguments.doc: The value of the upper edge of the Hermite function.

arguments.name: c
arguments.doc: The source value for interpolation.

doc: smoothstep> Performs smooth Hermite interpolation between `0` and `1` when a < c < b. This is useful in cases where a threshold function with a smooth transition is desired. Smoothstep is equivalent to: vec_type t; t = clamp((c - a) / (b - a), 0.0, 1.0); return t * t * (3.0 - 2.0 * t); Copy to clipboard Results are undefined if `a >= b`.

name: refract

return.doc: The refraction vector. vec_type *faceforward*(vec_type N, vec_type I, vec_type Nref) 🔗 <#shader-func-faceforward> Returns a vector pointing in the same direction as another. Orients a vector to point away from a surface as defined by its normal. If `dot(Nref, I) < 0` faceforward returns `N`, otherwise it returns `-N`. The oriented vector.

arguments.name: I
arguments.doc: The incident vector. The incident vector.

arguments.name: N
arguments.doc: The normal vector. The vector to orient.

arguments.name: eta
arguments.doc: The ratio of indices of refraction.

doc: Calculate the refraction direction for an incident vector. For a given incident vector `I`, surface normal `N` and ratio of indices of refraction, `eta`, refract returns the refraction vector, `R`. `R` is calculated as: k = 1.0 - eta * eta * (1.0 - dot(N, I) * dot(N, I)); if (k < 0.0) R = genType(0.0);       // or genDType(0.0) else R = eta * I - (eta * dot(N, I) + sqrt(k)) * N; Copy to clipboard Note The input parameters I and N should be normalized in order to achieve the desired result.

name: dFdx

arguments.name: p
arguments.doc: The expression of which to take the partial derivative. Note It is assumed that the expression `p` is continuous and therefore expressions evaluated via non-uniform control flow may be undefined.

doc: Note Available only in the fragment shader. Returns the partial derivative of `p` with respect to the window x coordinate using local differencing. Returns either dFdxCoarse <#shader-func-dfdxcoarse> or dFdxFine <#shader-func-dfdxfine>. The implementation may choose which calculation to perform based upon factors such as performance or the value of the API `GL_FRAGMENT_SHADER_DERIVATIVE_HINT` hint. Warning Expressions that imply higher order derivatives such as ` dFdx(dFdx(n))` have undefined results, as do mixed-order derivatives such as `dFdx(dFdy(n))`.

name: dFdxCoarse

arguments.name: p
arguments.doc: The expression of which to take the partial derivative. Note It is assumed that the expression `p` is continuous and therefore expressions evaluated via non-uniform control flow may be undefined.

doc: Note Available only in the fragment shader. Not available when using the Compatibility renderer. Returns the partial derivative of `p` with respect to the window x coordinate. Calculates derivatives using local differencing based on the value of `p` for the current fragment's neighbors, and will possibly, but not necessarily, include the value for the current fragment. That is, over a given area, the implementation can compute derivatives in fewer unique locations than would be allowed for the corresponding dFdxFine <#shader-func-dfdxfine> function. Warning Expressions that imply higher order derivatives such as ` dFdx(dFdx(n))` have undefined results, as do mixed-order derivatives such as `dFdx(dFdy(n))`.

doc: Converts two 32-bit floating-point quantities to 16-bit floating- point quantities and packs them into a single 32-bit integer. Returns an unsigned integer obtained by converting the components of a two-component floating-point vector to the 16-bit floating-point representation found in the OpenGL Specification, and then packing these two 16-bit integers into a 32-bit unsigned integer. The first vector component specifies the 16 least-significant bits of the result; the second component specifies the 16 most-significant bits.

The first component of the vector is obtained from the 16 least-significant bits of `v`; the second component is obtained from the 16 most-significant bits of `v`.

The conversion for component c of `v` to fixed-point is performed as follows: round(clamp(c, 0.0, 1.0) * 65535.0) Copy to clipboard The first component of the vector will be written to the least significant bits of the output; the last component will be written to the most significant bits.

doc: Find the index of the most significant bit set to 1. Note For signed integer types, the sign bit is checked first and then: * For positive integers, the result will be the bit number of the most significant bit that is set to 1. * For negative integers, the result will be the bit number of the most significant bit set to 0. Note For a value of zero or negative 1, -1 will be returned.
